question: Who became the first Indian boxer to win a gold medal at the World Boxing Cup in 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hitesh Gulia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hitesh Gulia** became the first Indian boxer to win a **gold medal** at the **World Boxing Cup in 2025**, making history and bringing immense pride to the nation.
 
• The **World Boxing Cup** is one of the most prestigious international boxing tournaments, where athletes from around the globe compete for top honors.
 
• Hitesh Gulia's victory showcased exceptional skill, determination, and preparation, marking a milestone in Indian boxing history.
 
• His win highlights the growing prominence of **Indian boxers** on the global stage, reflecting the advancements in training and support for sports in India.
 
• This achievement further inspires young athletes across the country to pursue boxing and other sports with dedication and passion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hitesh Gulia**:

 
 
• Hitesh Gulia is an emerging talent in Indian boxing, known for his **agility, precision, and powerful punches**.
 
• He hails from **Haryana**, a state that has produced numerous prominent athletes in India.
 
• Gulia's win at the **World Boxing Cup 2025** has set a benchmark for Indian boxers, proving their capability to excel at the international level.
 
• He competed in the **lightweight category** and defeated some of the best boxers in the world to secure the gold medal.
 
 
 
• **World Boxing Cup**:
 
 
• The World Boxing Cup is organized by the **International Boxing Association (IBA)** and is considered one of the toughest competitions in the sport.
 
• It features athletes from all over the world, competing across various weight categories.
 
• The event serves as a platform to showcase talent and often acts as a precursor to the **Olympics** and other major global competitions.
 
• Winning a gold medal at this event is a remarkable achievement, as it requires a combination of skill, strategy, and mental toughness.
 
 
 
• **Other Indian Boxing Achievements:**
 
 
• **Mary Kom**, a six-time world champion, has been a pioneer in Indian boxing and has inspired generations of boxers.
 
• **Amit Panghal** won a silver medal at the **2019 AIBA World Boxing Championships**, establishing himself as one of the top Indian boxers.
 
• **Shiva Thapa**, a highly celebrated Indian boxer, has won multiple medals at international events, including the Asian Championships.
 
• The success of these boxers has contributed to the growing popularity of boxing in India and has led to increased support for the sport.
 
 
 
• **India's Boxing Support System:**
 
 
• The **Boxing Federation of India (BFI)** plays a crucial role in organizing tournaments, training camps, and providing infrastructure for boxers.
 
• Government schemes such as **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)** provide financial and logistical support to elite athletes.
 
• Training facilities like the **National Boxing Academy in Rohtak** have been instrumental in nurturing talent.
 
• Collaboration with international coaches and exposure to global tournaments have significantly improved the performance of Indian boxers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India's Boxing Legacy:**

 
 
• Indian boxers have consistently performed well at events like the **Commonwealth Games**, **Asian Games**, and **Olympics**.
 
• **Vijender Singh** became the first Indian boxer to win an Olympic medal (bronze) in **2008 Beijing Olympics**.
 
• The rise of professional boxing leagues in India has further boosted the popularity of the sport.
 
 
 
• **Future of Indian Boxing:**
 
 
• With increasing investment in sports infrastructure and training, the future of Indian boxing looks promising.
 
• Young talents like **Hitesh Gulia** are expected to lead the next generation of Indian boxers on the global stage.
 
• Efforts to promote sports at the grassroots level are helping identify and nurture talent in rural and urban areas.
